title: An irrational-trace counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes
main_claim: There is a finitely generated group G=V⋊Γ, where Γ is a graphical small-cancellation group built from Osajda-labelled LPS expanders and V is an F_p-module obtained by imposing dual-code relations on every expander copy. Its reduced C*-algebra contains a projection b0=1_{0}(T) whose trace is sum_i p^{-k_i}, which is irrational. By Lück's Theorem 0.3, every class in the image of assembly has rational trace, so [b0] is not in that image and coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes surjectivity fails.
coverage:
Checked line by line:
- Diagram minimality and arc-count lemma: Euler/valence count gives b<=3F+3m-3, F/λ<=2b, so F<=m-1 and b<=6m.
- Avoidance bound 12(L+1)λσ, including why no bridge lies inside the designated side.
- Short-filling argument behind hyperbolicity: checked at the level of the structure of the argument.
- Overlap lemma: the thin-triangle walk length works out to exactly L0=2+2t+2D0, and the case d(A,R)<t is handled.
- Order of constants (D0, then λ, then the expanders): no circularity.
- Copy-cycle direct sum (Lemma 3.2).
- Code lemma: the probabilities and the union bound are right; numerically H2(0.01)=0.0808 and the bound is about 1e-12 at n=101, p=3.
- Exact module intersection W0∩F_p^P=C_P^⊥ with root at c_P, and the uniform marginals p^{-k_i}.
- Covariance and enabled-edge formula for π_ω, and the trace integral.
- Valid copies are isolated components and pairwise disjoint.
- Local deficit (expansion case vs mismatch case).
- Global cycle-rank charging: elimination identity, support of the projected cycle in B_P∪(A∩P), the tree-attachment rank formula, girth separation σ-2r-2>σ/2, packing l_C<=4|C|/σ, 5/σ<c/4, and that the charged exterior sets are disjoint even with ties.
- Cheeger layer-cake and Cauchy–Schwarz bound giving c^2/(8d).
- Spectrum passes through the faithful direct sum of the π_ω.
- Trace count: n_i copies through the identity, each contributing (1/n_i)p^{-k_i}.
- Irrationality: base-p digits with gaps tending to infinity.
- Use of Lück's Λ^G statement.

Not independently verified (external inputs trusted):
- Osajda's Theorem 2.7 hypotheses and conclusion (C'(λ) uniqueness of simple paths, isometric embedding).
- That Bridson–Haefliger III.H.2.9 gives a universal hyperbolicity constant from the stated coarse-filling construction.
- Exact wording of Lück's Theorem 0.3.
